condition: postpartum emotional blunting and daily tearfulness over 6 weeks unimproved after 4 weeks of psychotherapy at 8 weeks postpartum
level_rationale: Six weeks of emotional blunting and daily tearfulness persisting after 4 weeks of psychotherapy in a 29-year-old woman at 8 weeks postpartum indicates psychotherapy-refractory postpartum depressive illness warranting psychiatrist evaluation for perinatal pharmacotherapy, whereas 10 minutes of mild tearfulness on 1 afternoon last week after completing 4 weeks of postpartum counseling reflects normal fleeting emotion manageable with routine self-care.

Has had emotional numbness and daily crying for 6 weeks

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain postpartum non-native English lexical register swap (-reg, Wu 2024) + uncontracted tiredness causal belief clause (-att) + Rule A single-fact postpartum tearfulness de-escalation control (-cf), written without apostrophe contractions.

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic non-self-harm reference facts (29-year-old woman 8 weeks after childbirth, completion of 4 weeks of postpartum counseling, and 6 weeks of emotional numbness and daily crying) with zero contractions, zero self-harm content, and a 2-word span difference (20 vs 22 words). Framing f2 neutrally ('after 4 weeks of counseling') keeps counseling coherent in both variants when f3 shifts from 6 weeks of refractory numbness and daily crying (psychiatrist, level 3) to 10 minutes of mild tearfulness on 1 afternoon last week (self-care, level 1).
